summary: Samuel Johnson worked in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (around 1725–1726), and Pembroke College (1728–1731).
Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Wells Williams was a scholar in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (around 1831–1832) and held a post at Yale University from around 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at San Diego State University, where she is attested as a professor in 1999 and as an associate professor of philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and also held an academic post there.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and wrote her MA thesis under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Sang-Kyun Sun is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995). That same year, he held a post as lecturer at Jingak Sangha University.

Sangay Dorji works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tengtho Goenpa and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies, taught Gembo Dorji, and held posts as teacher at Simtokha Dzong and Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

Sangharakshita was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1950) and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Jianmin Chen, and Dhardo Rinpoche. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi and Delhi School of Economics. He has held chairs at Oxford, the Collège de France, and UCLA, and taught at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Sanjaya Lall was educated at St. Xavier's High School, Patna, and St John's College, Oxford (~1960–1965). He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1970 until 2005.
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher A. P. Lama and under teacher and guide Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya (attested 1994).

Sanjukta Gupta is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned degrees from Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Jadavpur, Utrecht University (~1971–1986), and the University of Oxford (~1986–2000).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. In Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).

Sara L. McClintock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who earned her PhD from Harvard (-2002). She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and Emory University, where she is associate professor of religion.
Sarah Aoife Richardson works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2016 under the supervision of Jennifer Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University. She held posts at Northwestern University (associate professor, 1996) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale University (~1995–1999) and the University of Virginia (~2001–2007), later holding posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (starting 2009).
